data.summary: The pod startup exceeded its SLO of 10.0 s, taking 52.0 s to become Ready. The primary cause was a cold image pull of a large 648 MB image, which took 48.954 s. This phase accounted for 94.1% of the total startup time.

findings.statement: The total startup time for the pod was 52.0 s, exceeding the SLO threshold of 10.0 s.
The image pull phase was the longest, lasting 48.954 s, which represents 94.1% of the total startup time.
The image being pulled is large, with a size of 647991705 bytes (approximately 648 MB).
The image pull occurred during a cold start.
The image pull throughput was 13236747 bytes/s (approximately 13.2 MB/s), which is a normal rate for a large image.

ruled_out.reason: The image pull throughput of 13.2 MB/s is considered normal and does not indicate a slow registry or network issue.
There was no time spent on model loading, as indicated by a model_s duration of 0.0 s.
Application initialisation took only 1.089 s, which is a small fraction of the total startup time.
The pod did not experience any scheduling delays, with a scheduling duration of 0.0 s and no failed scheduling events.
The readiness probe phase took only 0.691 s, and there were no probe failures after the application was ready.

recommendations.rationale: Reducing the image size will decrease the time required for image pulls, especially during cold starts, thereby improving startup performance.
Caching frequently used images on worker nodes can significantly reduce image pull times for subsequent pod starts on the same node.
